sections.html:
Faux amis ("false friends") are French words that look like English words but have a different meaning. They cause some of the most common mistakes.

French Actually means Not English word → French
actuellement currently actually actually → en fait
assister à to attend to assist to assist → aider
attendre to wait to attend to attend → assister à
blesser to injure to bless to bless → bénir
bras arm bra bra → soutien-gorge
caractère temperament character (in a story) character → personnage
chance luck chance chance → occasion / possibilité
collège middle school college college → cégep (Qc) / université
commander to order (food) to command
crayon pencil crayon crayon → crayon de cire / de couleur
déception disappointment deception deception → tromperie
demander to ask to demand to demand → exiger
éventuellement possibly eventually eventually → finalement
excité (often) aroused, overexcited excited (happy) excited → enthousiaste / j'ai hâte
formidable great, wonderful formidable (fearsome)
gentil kind, nice gentle gentle → doux
journée day journey journey → voyage / trajet
librairie bookstore library library → bibliothèque
location rental location location → endroit / lieu
monnaie change (coins), currency money money → argent
passer un examen to take an exam to pass an exam to pass → réussir un examen
préservatif condom preservative preservative → conservateur
rester to stay to rest to rest → se reposer
sensible sensitive sensible sensible → raisonnable
sympathique nice, friendly sympathetic sympathetic → compatissant
travailler to work to travel to travel → voyager
user to wear out to use to use → utiliser
veste jacket vest vest → gilet
raisin grape raisin raisin → raisin sec
lecture reading lecture lecture → conférence / cours magistral
avertissement warning advertisement advertisement → publicité
coin corner coin coin → pièce de monnaie

sections.heading: Most embarrassing ones
sections.html:
• Je suis excité ! can sound sexual. Say J'ai hâte ! (I can't wait) or Je suis enthousiaste**.
  • Je suis plein(e) (I'm full after eating) can mean pregnant (animal) or drunk. Say J'ai bien mangé* / Je n'ai plus faim*.
  • Un préservatif** is a condom, not a food preservative.

exercises.answer: *J'ai tellement hâte de faire ce voyage !*
